Analytical Breakdowns

A running log of 1,087 data-driven breakdowns and counting — five highlights below, each walking through the trend, the numbers behind it, and how it played out.

12/13/2024  —  LAC @ DEN  —  Ivica Zubac  —  Assists O1.5
Hit  ·  4 AST

Reading Denver's pick-and-roll coverage

Denver's defensive scheme against opposing centers in the pick-and-roll created a repeatable pattern this season: with Jokic limited in space, the Nuggets shifted to tagging the roll man from the weak-side corner — opening a short-roll 2-on-1 that consistently fed easy assists to opposing bigs.

Cross-referencing recent center-vs-Jokic assist logs and Denver's second-chance/offensive-rebound rates (top of the league) pointed to a favorable setup for Zubac's assist line specifically, independent of his season average.

2024 NBA FINALS  —  GM 3 · BOS vs DAL  —  Jaylen Brown  —  Assists O3.5
Hit  ·  8 AST

Attacking mismatches forces the assist number up

Boston's offense in this series ran through driving lanes created by switch-heavy mismatches, and Jaylen Brown was the team's primary driver — leading the roster in drives and makes off drives across the season and playoffs. With Boston's five-out spacing leaving Dallas's help defense only one pass away, Brown could generate an open look almost immediately after beating his man off the dribble.

Boston leaned further into the drive-and-kick approach between Games 1 and 2, and Brown's passes off drives rose accordingly. Combined with a heavy share of his assists coming off threes, the setup pointed to a strong assist number independent of his usual playmaking role.

2025 NBA FINALS  —  GM 5 · OKC vs IND  —  Jalen Williams  —  Points O22.5
Hit  ·  40 PTS

Usage spike makes the number stale

Jalen Williams had already covered this points line in back-to-back Finals games as his usage rate climbed under Indiana's defensive pressure on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. With Williams operating as a primary ball handler even when Shai was on the floor, Indiana's coverage was consistently giving him a runway downhill — reflected in a heavy free-throw rate over his last two outings.

OKC also began using Shai as a screener for Williams, opening driving lanes that were likely to keep generating easy interior looks. Between the usage trend and the shot-volume pattern, the posted line looked behind where his role in the series had actually moved.

WCF  —  GM 3 · MIN vs DAL  —  P.J. Washington  —  Points O11.5
Hit  ·  16 PTS

A coverage gap hiding in plain sight

Dallas's staggered pick-and-roll in Game 2 let their bigs get downhill because Minnesota's defense was blitzing the primary ball handlers without tagging the roller from the weakside corner, where Washington was consistently stationed. Minnesota's frustration with that rotation gap was visible on the floor, but the pattern hadn't been fixed by tip-off.

Washington was also getting live pick-and-pop reps, screening for Dallas's guards while Minnesota left him open to double the ball handler. Volume was already there — he'd cleared 10+ field goal attempts in both games of the series — even with his 3-point efficiency dipped from earlier rounds.

2026 NBA PLAYOFFS  —  76ers vs Celtics  —  VJ Edgecombe  —  FGM O5
Hit  ·  12 FGM

Volume finds him even off the ball

With Maxey and George on the floor and Embiid out, Edgecombe has averaged a heavy shot diet per 36 minutes and had already hit this same line in both postseason games so far. Boston's drop coverage has started shading extra help toward Maxey at the nail before peeling back into perimeter switches — a scheme built to force jumpers from weaker shooters.

Edgecombe is usually positioned exactly one pass away from that action, which lets him find open threes or attack closeouts off the ball, plus pick up pull-up looks against the weaker defender left on him in pick-and-rolls and dribble handoffs. Boston's low shooting-foul rate on top of that meant volume was likely to come from the field rather than the line.

About

Sidd Gautam

I'm a private tutor and University of Georgia graduate working to break into the sports industry — specifically team operations and data analytics. As a lifelong NBA fan, I'm drawn to how front offices are built, how data informs decision-making, and what it takes to run a successful organization on and off the court.

I was selected as one of 140 students nationwide for Sports Business Classroom's Business of Basketball Immersive Experience during NBA Summer League, focusing on the Collective Bargaining Agreement & Salary Cap track — evaluating trades, contracts, and roster-building strategy.
